addedMass.note: Diagonal of the added-mass matrix from Prestero (2001): a slender body, so sway and heave carry far more entrained water than surge.

linearDamping.note: Prestero models the drag as quadratic; the linear terms are small and are carried so that the model settles rather than oscillating at very low speed.

quadraticDamping.note: Cross-flow and axial drag coefficients from Prestero (2001).

thrusters.note: A torpedo: one propeller on the axis and four fins. Only the propeller is a thruster in the sense this platform allocates; the fins steer by deflection at speed, which the allocator does not model yet. Until it does, this vehicle can go forward and cannot turn.

sensors.name: bottom_track
sensors.wattsNote: a Nortek DVL1000, averaged over its ping

sensors.name: body
sensors.wattsNote: a MEMS unit; a fibre-optic gyro is ten times this

sensors.name: depth
sensors.wattsNote: a pressure sensor, which costs nothing

sensors.name: side_scan
sensors.wattsNote: a Blueprint Oculus, which is most of what a small ROV's hotel load is when it is on

sensors.name: ctd
sensors.note: Conductivity, temperature and depth. The instrument every oceanographic vehicle carries and the reason a glider section is worth flying.
sensors.wattsNote: a pumped SBE 49, which is why gliders can carry one

subscribes.note: One normalised command in [-1, 1] for the propeller.

modem.note: The same micro-modem class link as the BlueROV2.

power.hotelNote: The base electronics and nothing else: the vehicle computer and its housekeeping. It was a single lumped figure that stood for the electronics, the sensors and the lights together — which meant unfitting a Doppler log or switching the lamps off changed the endurance by exactly nothing. Each instrument states its own draw now and they are added to this, so a dive that carries less lasts longer, which is the whole reason to be able to choose.

computer.note: A survey AUV's own computer: navigation, logging, and the payload.
